title: Citroën C4 Grand Picasso Technical Workshop Dataset

procedures.title: Alternator Removal & Auxiliary Drive Servicing
procedures.summary: Step-by-step complete removal of the 150A alternator on the PSA 1.6 HDi (DV6TED4/DV6C) engine. Details auxiliary drive de-tensioning, power steering pump relocation without hydraulic disconnection, bolt sequencing, and extraction angles past the front wheel arch.
safetyNotes: DISCONNECT NEGATIVE BATTERY TERMINAL: The B+ lead to the alternator carries unfused direct battery voltage.
BSI SLEEP PROTOCOL: Open bonnet, close all vehicle doors, remove ignition key, and wait a strict minimum of 3 minutes before unhooking the battery clamp.
AXLE STANDS MANDATORY: Never work under the vehicle supported only by a hydraulic floor jack.

toolsNeeded.name: Plastic Trim & Clip Removal Pry Bar

torqueSpecs.notes: Torque progressively to maintain bracket alignment.
Do not overtighten to avoid cracking alternator diode bridge insulator.
Ensure locating lug is seated in engine casing recess.

steps.title: BSI Sleep Protocol & Battery Disconnection
steps.instructions: Park vehicle on level ground. Open the bonnet. Roll down driver window (prevents lockout). Turn ignition off, remove key, and ensure all doors remain closed. Wait at least 3 minutes to allow the Body System Interface (BSI) to write adaptive memory and enter deep sleep. Release the quick-release negative battery terminal clamp and stow the cable safely away from the battery post.
steps.warning: Prematurely disconnecting the battery can corrupt BSI configuration and immobilizer data.
steps.caution: The alternator B+ cable carries live battery current if the terminal is not disconnected.

steps.title: Front Right Wheel & Arch Splash Guard Removal
steps.instructions: Loosen front right wheel bolts slightly. Jack up the right front corner at the reinforced sill jacking notch. Secure vehicle firmly onto an axle stand. Remove wheel. Remove the plastic expanding push-rivets and 10mm screws securing the front half of the wheel arch inner plastic liner. Fold back or remove the liner to expose the lower crankshaft pulley and auxiliary belt run.

steps.title: Engine Undertray Removal
steps.instructions: Underneath the front bumper, remove the 10mm perimeter hex bolts and T20 Torx fasteners holding the lower acoustic engine tray. Slide the tray backward and unhook from the front subframe lip.

steps.title: Auxiliary Drive Belt De-Tensioning & Removal
steps.instructions: Locate the dynamic belt tensioner (between crankshaft pulley and alternator). Fit a 15mm offset ring spanner onto the central hex head of the tensioner roller. Pull the spanner firmly clockwise (towards front of car) against spring tension until the 4mm locking hole aligns with the engine block recess. Insert a 4mm pin or hex key into the locking hole. Slip the 6PK1070 ribbed belt off the alternator and crankshaft pulleys.
steps.caution: Inspect the belt for cracking and inspect the alternator overrunning freewheel clutch (it should rotate freely in one direction and lock in the other).

steps.title: Power Steering Pump Reservoir Relocation
steps.instructions: On Mk1 1.6 HDi models with power steering reservoir/bracket mounted in the upper right bay, remove the 2x 10mm retaining bolts. Gently lift and tilt the reservoir aside and secure with a bungee cord. DO NOT disconnect the hydraulic hoses.

steps.title: Alternator Electrical Disconnections
steps.instructions: Reach behind the rear plastic casing of the alternator. Squeeze the locking tab on the 2-pin excitation/LIN communication wiring harness plug and pull straight out. Flip back the protective rubber boot on the B+ positive stud. Use a 13mm socket to unthread the M8 retaining nut and slide off the heavy copper power terminal cable.
steps.caution: Protect the ring terminal with insulating tape to prevent accidental shorting on chassis metal.

steps.title: Alternator Mounting Bolts Removal
steps.instructions: Using a 13mm socket with extension, loosen and remove the two upper M10 mounting bolts (front and rear). Then, through the lower wheel arch opening, loosen and extract the long lower M10 pivot bolt. Gently rock the alternator on its dowels with a small pry bar to free it from the aluminum bracket sleeves.

steps.title: Extraction & Reassembly Torque Specifications
steps.instructions: Maneuver the alternator downward and outward through the space between the subframe, right wheel arch inner edge, and lower radiator hose. On installation: slide new alternator into mounting lugs; finger-tighten lower pivot bolt first, followed by upper bolts. Torque lower and upper mounting bolts to 40 Nm. Torque B+ nut to 15 Nm. Refit auxiliary belt according to the serpentine routing schematic. Rotate tensioner to release the 4mm locking pin. Reconnect battery and let vehicle idle for 2 minutes before testing charge voltage (target: 14.1V - 14.4V).

procedures.title: Fuel Filter Replacement & Hand Primer Bleeding
procedures.summary: Replacement of the metal canister fuel filter on top of the DV6 engine. Explains push-fit fuel line union release, water-in-fuel sensor swap, and manual priming using the integrated rubber primer bulb.
safetyNotes: FIRE SAFETY: Place lint-free shop rags beneath unions to catch diesel spills.
AIR BLEED MANDATORY: The common-rail high-pressure pump (Bosch CP1H) is lubricated solely by diesel; never crank an unprimed dry system.

torqueSpecs.notes: Snug only to prevent cracking plastic body.

steps.title: Acoustic Engine Cover Removal
steps.instructions: Pull upward on the four rubber ball mounts of the plastic engine top cover to release it.

steps.title: Fuel Line Quick-Release Unions
steps.instructions: Squeeze the white/green plastic side tabs on the fuel inlet and outlet quick-connect couplings and slide off cleanly.

steps.title: Filter Bracket & Sensor Transfer
steps.instructions: Unhook the electric fuel heater harness plug and remove the canister from its mounting bracket. Transfer water sensor to new filter.

steps.title: Priming Bulb Operation
steps.instructions: Reconnect fuel lines. Repeatedly squeeze the rubber hand primer bulb located on the top left of the engine until firm resistance is felt. Start engine and check for leaks.

procedures.title: Rear Air Suspension Spring (Pneumatic Bellows) Replacement
procedures.summary: Servicing leaking rear pneumatic air suspension bags on Grand Picasso Exclusive models. Details vehicle suspension deflation, push-fit brass airline disconnection, top retaining clip, and calibration.
safetyNotes: DEPRESSURIZE AIR SYSTEM FIRST: High pressure air (up to 9 bar) can cause injury if airline is released while pressurized.
SUPPORT AXLE: The rear trailing arm will drop once the pneumatic bag is unseated.

steps.title: Air Suspension Depressurization
steps.instructions: Locate the manual boot switch or use a diagnostic tool to fully lower the rear suspension to dump bag pressure. Disconnect battery.

steps.title: Jack Rear Axle & Remove Wheel
steps.instructions: Raise rear of car, place on heavy chassis stands, and remove the rear wheel.

steps.title: Disconnect Pneumatic Airline
steps.instructions: Push the brass collet ring inwards while pulling the 4mm nylon airline tube outwards to release the push-fit union.

steps.title: Bellows Twist & Disengage
steps.instructions: Twist the rubber air spring 90 degrees counter-clockwise to disengage the bayonet locking lugs from the axle perch. Install new bag.

procedures.title: Fuse Box Layouts & Electrical Diagnostics (Mk1 2006–2013)
procedures.summary: Full technical fuse allocation maps for 2010 Citroën C4 Grand Picasso (StartMyCar verified). Covers Dashboard Cabin Box (BSI1), Under-Bonnet Engine Box (BSM), and Battery-Top Distribution Unit (BPGA). Instant diagnostic lookup for 12V sockets (F9), Air Suspension (F10/MF3), Starter Relay (F8), OBD Port (F4), and Washer Pump (F3).
safetyNotes: ALWAYS DISCONNECT IGNITION: Turn off ignition and remove key before inspecting or pulling any fuse.
EXACT AMPERAGE REPLACEMENT: Never substitute a blown fuse with a higher amperage fuse or makeshift jumper wire; this can destroy the BSI microprocessor board or cause vehicle fire.
USE FUSE PULLER CLIP: Always use the plastic fuse extraction tweezer clipped inside the dashboard fusebox lid to avoid shorting adjacent terminals.

steps.title: Dashboard Fuse Box Access (RHD & LHD Differences)
steps.instructions: For UK/RHD models: Open the lower glovebox on the passenger side, rotate the single quarter-turn plastic fastener 90 degrees, and pivot the whole fuse panel assembly downwards. For LHD models: Unclip the lower driver dashboard flap by pulling the top-right and top-left corners downward.
steps.caution: Do not yank the panel; delicate ribbon cables connect to the BSI.

steps.title: Cabin Primary Fuses (F1 to F9: 12V Sockets & Accessories)
steps.instructions: F1 (15A Blue): Rear wiper. F2 (30A Green): Central door locking earth. F3 (5A Beige): Airbags & pretensioners. F4 (10A Red): OBD Diagnostic port, electrochrome mirror, A/C. F5 (30A Green): Front electric windows & panoramic roof. F6 (30A Green): Rear electric windows. F7 (5A Beige): Courtesy dome lamps & glovebox cooler. F8 (20A Yellow): Multifunction matrix display & audio. F9 (30A Green): FRONT 12V SOCKET / CIGARETTE LIGHTER & boot torch.

steps.title: Cabin Secondary Fuses (F10 to F17: Suspension & Gearbox)
steps.instructions: F10 (15A Blue): Rear pneumatic suspension height corrector ECU. F11 (15A Blue): Brake pedal switch & steering lock. F12 (15A Blue): Parking sensors, rain/light sensor, AFIL lane departure. F13 (5A Beige): BSM engine service supply & electric seats. F14 (15A Blue): EGS robotized gearbox selector & Bluetooth kit. F15 (30A Green): Central locking actuators. F17 (40A Orange): Heated rear window defroster.

steps.title: Engine Bay Fuse Box (BSM - Next to Battery)
steps.instructions: Open bonnet, locate the black plastic box directly to the right of the main battery casing, and release the two side retaining clips. Lift the cover upwards.

steps.title: Engine Bay Circuit Protection (BSM F1 to F10)
steps.instructions: F1 (20A Yellow): Engine management ECU. F2 (15A Blue): Dual tone horn. F3 (10A Red): Front & rear windscreen washer pump. F4 (20A Yellow): Headlamp high-pressure washer jets. F5 (15A Blue): Fuel vaporiser & emission solenoids. F6 (10A Red): Bi-xenon directional headlights & clutch safety switch. F7 (10A Red): EGS gearbox ECU & power steering ECU logic. F8 (20A Yellow): STARTER MOTOR SOLENOID RELAY. F9 (10A Red): Dual brake switch logic.
steps.caution: If starter clicks but engine does not crank, inspect F8 (20A) in the BSM.

steps.title: Battery Top Power Distribution Unit (BPGA Maxi Fuses)
steps.instructions: Lift the red positive battery clamp shield to access the bolted mega fuses: MF1 (50A): Radiator cooling fan. MF2 (80A): Electro-hydraulic power steering pump. MF3 (40A): REAR PNEUMATIC AIR SUSPENSION COMPRESSOR. MF4 (80A): Main cabin BSI feed. MF5 (80A): ESP/ABS hydraulic pump module.
steps.warning: These are live unfused battery terminals. Use insulated tools only.

diagnosticEcus.description: Standard emissions-related broadcast to all powertrain nodes
PSA Common Rail Diesel Engine ECU for DV6 1.6 HDi and DW10 2.0 HDi
Central comfort, lighting, security, and immobilizer gateway
Rear axle pneumatic height corrector and 12V air compressor controller
Robotized clutch actuator and hydraulic pressure pump controller

dtcDefinitions.title: Preheating Relay Circuit (Glow Plugs Not Supplied)
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: The preheating control unit receives power but detects an open circuit to one or more glow plugs. Very common on 1.6 HDi (DV6); does not illuminate the Check Engine Light (MIL).
commonCauses: One or more burnt glow plugs (high internal resistance)
Preheating relay contacts corroded (under battery tray)
Glow plug wiring harness damaged or loose terminal connector

dtcDefinitions.title: Preheating Relay Circuit (Relay Supplied / Control Discrepancy)
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Engine management ECU detected coherence failure between commanded glow plug state and relay feedback.
commonCauses: Defective preheat relay unit
Blown preheat supply fuse in engine BSM / battery distribution unit
Earth connection fault on engine block

dtcDefinitions.title: EGR Valve Position Sensor (Stuck Open / Flow Mismatch)
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: The exhaust gas recirculation valve potentiometer signal does not match the commanded lift position during deceleration or regeneration.
commonCauses: Heavy carbon soot jamming Valeo EGR pintle valve
EGR valve electrical actuator motor gear wear
Faulty EGR position sensor wiring

dtcDefinitions.title: Turbocharger Underboost (Boost Pressure Below Threshold)
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Measured manifold absolute pressure (MAP) is lower than target boost pressure by more than 300 mbar for over 5 seconds under load.
commonCauses: Split turbo intercooler air doser rubber hose (common behind radiator)
Turbo electro-pneumatic vacuum control solenoid valve failed
Vacuum hose cracked, perished, or detached from wastegate actuator
Turbocharger variable nozzle (VNT) mechanism carbonized and binding

dtcDefinitions.title: Turbocharger Overboost Condition
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Charge air pressure exceeded maximum safe threshold. Engine may enter limp-home mode to protect intercooler and pistons.
commonCauses: Variable vane geometry sticking in high boost position
Turbo vacuum solenoid stuck venting to atmospheric pressure
Faulty MAP sensor signal reading high

dtcDefinitions.title: Reversible Alternator / Drive Belt Slip (Stop-Start / Charging)
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Alternator excitation or freewheel clutch pulley slippage detected. Charging voltage intermittent or belt tensioner loose.
commonCauses: Seized alternator freewheel overrunning clutch pulley (OAP)
Auxiliary drive belt slack or dynamic tensioner damper worn out
Alternator internal voltage regulator brush wear (150A Valeo/Mitsubishi)

dtcDefinitions.title: System Charging Voltage Low (< 10.5V)
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Engine ECU battery sense line drops below minimum operating voltage while engine is running.
commonCauses: Failing alternator assembly or worn brushes
Slack auxiliary drive belt slipping under electrical load
Corroded battery earth strap or blown BPGA maxi fuse

dtcDefinitions.title: System Charging Voltage High (> 15.8V)
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Alternator internal voltage regulator failure causing dangerous over-voltage to vehicle microprocessors.
commonCauses: Alternator diode pack or regulator shorted internally
Loose B+ alternator output cable nut (13mm)

dtcDefinitions.title: Engine Starting / Stopping Controlled by Engine ECU Discrepancy
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Engine ECU received starting command not synchronized with BSI immobilizer key transponder authorization.
commonCauses: Low battery voltage during cranking causing BSI reboot
Ignition switch contact bounce (Neiman switch)
Starter motor solenoid drawing excessive current

dtcDefinitions.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Below Minimum Setpoint
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Common rail pressure drops below target rail pressure under heavy acceleration.
commonCauses: Blocked diesel fuel filter (high restriction)
High pressure fuel pump flow regulator valve sticking
Excessive injector spill back (leak-off)

dtcDefinitions.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Exceeded Setpoint
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Measured common rail pressure higher than commanded limit. High pressure safety limiter opened.
commonCauses: Common rail pressure regulator valve stuck closed
Fuel rail pressure sensor calibration drifted

dtcDefinitions.title: DPF Additive Quantity Injected Into Filter Exceeded Limit
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Additive fluid dosing counter has reached theoretical maximum filter capacity. FAP soot filter service required.
commonCauses: DPF particulate filter loaded with non-burnable cerine ash
Additive pump counter requires reset after physical filter clean

dtcDefinitions.title: DPF Additive (EOLYS) Reservoir Empty
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Additive level sensor in the additive pouch/tank under the vehicle has detected empty fluid condition.
commonCauses: EOLYS / Powerflex additive fluid exhausted in tank
Additive level sensor float switch stuck

dtcDefinitions.title: Fuel Tank Filler Cap Sensor Circuit Coherence
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Reed switch sensor on the fuel filler neck cannot detect the magnet on the fuel cap. Additive dosing suspended.
commonCauses: Magnet missing from aftermarket replacement fuel cap
Fuel filler cap sensor reed switch wiring broken near fuel tank

dtcDefinitions.title: Air Compressor Max Runtime Exceeded (Thermal Protection)
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: 12V air suspension compressor ran continuously for over 180 seconds trying to reach target chassis ride height. Thermal cut-off triggered.
commonCauses: Perished rear pneumatic rubber spring bellows leaking air under load
Split 4mm nylon airline tube near rear suspension arm pivot
Compressor piston ring worn, producing insufficient flow (< 5 bar)

dtcDefinitions.title: Air Suspension Solenoid Valve Leak / Pressure Drop
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Chassis height drops when air valves are closed. Uncommanded deflation detected.
commonCauses: Pneumatic bellows puncture or micro-porosity along bottom rubber fold
Brass push-fit airline union seal leaking
Solenoid valve manifold internal seal contamination

dtcDefinitions.title: Rear Right Height Sensor Voltage Coherence Error
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Sensor output voltage outside allowable physical travel range (0.5V to 4.5V).
commonCauses: Height sensor plastic linkage arm ball joint popped off trailing arm
Sensor internal resistive track water corroded
Sensor harness unplugged or pinched

dtcDefinitions.title: Rear Left Height Sensor Voltage Coherence Error
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Sensor output voltage outside allowable physical travel range (0.5V to 4.5V).
commonCauses: Height sensor linkage ball joint popped off axle arm
Sensor water ingress
Wiring harness damage

dtcDefinitions.title: Clutch Actuator Position Sensor Signal Coherence
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Discrepancy between commanded clutch release position and actual position reported by Hall effect sensor.
commonCauses: Clutch release bearing guide sleeve sticky or dry of grease
Clutch friction plate worn to rivets, causing clutch judder
Hydraulic slave cylinder internal seal leakage
EGS6 clutch bite-point calibration adaptation needed

dtcDefinitions.title: Hydraulic Circuit Pressure Loss (EGS6 Pump Unit)
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Hydraulic pressure drops below 35 bar while vehicle is in gear. Gearbox shifts to neutral for safety.
commonCauses: Hydraulic pressure accumulator nitrogen sphere diaphragm failed
Electric hydraulic pump motor relay or brushes worn
Low Tutela CS Speed fluid level in EGS actuator reservoir

dtcDefinitions.title: Hydraulic Fluid Pressure Low (< 38 Bar)
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Hydraulic pump running excessively without reaching cutoff pressure (48 bar).
commonCauses: Hydraulic pump electric motor failing
Accumulator sphere lost charge
Fluid leak from actuator block unions

dtcDefinitions.title: Brake Pedal Switch Signal Coherence For Gear Selection
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: Dual brake switch contacts (normally open / normally closed) do not switch simultaneously. EGS prevents shifting into D/R.
commonCauses: Faulty four-pin brake light switch above brake pedal
Brake switch ratchet clip out of adjustment

dtcDefinitions.title: BSI Internal Power Supply / Microprocessor Wake-Up Error
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: BSI main computer suffered severe transient voltage drop during engine start or sleep transition.
commonCauses: Weak 12V vehicle battery (< 11.8V resting)
High starter motor current draw dragging system voltage
Loose battery positive terminal quick-release clamp

dtcDefinitions.title: Remote Key Wake-up Synchronization Error
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: High frequency key fob waking signal received without matching transponder immobilizer handshake.
commonCauses: Weak CR1620 battery in remote key fob
Key transponder antenna coil around ignition barrel intermittent
Radio frequency interference

dtcDefinitions.title: Trailer Relay Module (BSG) Lost on CAN Bus
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: BSI configured for trailer module but receives no CAN acknowledgement frame.
commonCauses: 13-pin trailer socket water ingress causing short circuit
Trailer module fuse blown in boot fuse panel (F12)
Aftermarket towbar wiring harness disconnected

dtcDefinitions.title: Dynamic Vehicle Speed Frame Received From ABS Invalid
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: ABS/ESP ECU broadcast invalid speed value on CAN network.
commonCauses: ABS wheel speed sensor magnetic target ring corroded on rear hub
Low battery voltage causing ABS transient communication drop

dtcDefinitions.title: CAN Communication Lost With BSI Body Computer
dtcDefinitions.technicalDescription: CAN network timeout between Engine ECU and BSI.
commonCauses: Engine bay wiring harness chafing under air filter box
BSI 3-minute sleep protocol violated during battery reconnection
